$comment: DecisionBook's words, as data: every code with what a person or an agent reads, and the lines its views say. contracts/codes.cjs is their one door.
codes: READY: the rubric holds and the plan is recorded
not READY: the rubric names what is missing

closing a teammate's plan ends their open work, so a person closes it, never an AI session: the task here is planned beside it with its own `atlasbound decisionbook new`; where the person wants it closed, they run atlasbound decisionbook close <id> in their terminal
nothing to record yet: no commit of this plan and no changed file of it
a plan is closed on its own branch as it was when the work was done: only there is HEAD's line its own work, so nothing is recorded here

since the plan's head, HEAD's line holds a commit that another branch's line holds too (a sync after a merge, a copy, a branch cut from it and a fast-forward merge of it all leave the same lines, so git cannot tell whose the commit is). So the plan's own commits are unknown and nothing is recorded. Each route is behind a condition the person can check. A route that moves the branch brings it back to the tip it left. A shape nothing can close is a lesson for next time, never an action
a decision was recorded as the person's: its "said" is their own words

"said" quotes the person: words of a message they typed in this session, as written (the product keeps the whole sentence they stand in; a confirm's, from a message after the plan and after any answer that keeps a decision, never one that keeps; a compared link's, their answer to the item, from a message after the line it names). Copy them from their message and send this again; a decision of your own is "whose":"assumed"; what they have not typed, ask them in plain words

a question goes to someone else only where something names them as the one who answers it: "source" says where (the issue or comment that names its owner, a document, a file:line, the person's sentence that said to ask them); with no such source it is the person's question: send it without "to"
a decision says whose words it holds: "whose": "person" (the person working here), a teammate's name, or "assumed" (no one stated it: your own choice), with "said" their exact words unless assumed
someone else's standing decision is replaced only on the person's words that name it, or on their answer to a question that showed it to them, never on a blanket answer
an answer with no "value" takes its question's proposal as it is, and this question proposed nothing: add "value", what you understood they decided
putting a question off is the person's: "said" quotes their own words that put it off, from a message they typed in this session; if they have not said so, ask them
a question is put off under its "q", and this plan asks no question of that name
words the person did not type are someone else's only where DecisionBook read them itself: in a comment or an issue at its address, or on a committed line of this repository

words the person typed are a teammate's only where the message's format names that teammate as the speaker (a chat line "Emma: …" and its lines, a chat header of a name and a time, the > lines under "Emma wrote:"), or where the person allowed them on the host's permission prompt for the add that records them; anything else they typed is their own words

a record of the person's carries their name, and none is kept for them on this machine: the person runs atlasbound whoami --name "<their name>" once in their own terminal (atlasbound setup keeps the name git gives), then this call is sent again
only the person replaces a person's decision: send the decision that replaces it as theirs ("whose":"person", "said": their own words that change it), or take it out of "supersedes"
a person's answer places each standing decision the question it answers names: "supersedes":["<ref>"] where their answer replaces it, "keeps":["<ref>"] where they keep it
a decision named in both "supersedes" and "keeps" is placed nowhere: name it in the one their answer means, never both

a keep takes the kept line's decision as it is, so this answer's "value" is that line's value, copied letter for letter. Where the person decided something else than that line says, they kept nothing: name it in "supersedes" with every other line

a keep stands beside the decision it keeps: under that decision's own key in its own plan (with "keeps", or as its value said again once the plan is READY) it would take the line's place and keep nothing, and a teammate's replacement of it would meet no conflict. Where the person said it stays, send it again under a key of its own (<key>.kept) with "keeps":["<this decision>"]
only the person keeps a standing decision: send the answer that keeps it as theirs ("whose":"person", "said": their own words that keep it), or take "keeps" out
a later session goes on with the draft an earlier one left open: its first add to it
a protected file outside the READY plan: open a new plan for this file with one `atlasbound decisionbook new`, or ask the person: their yes to this edit (Edit or Write) adds the file to the plan
a decision of this READY plan lost a conflict after the plan was built and edited, so the code may not match what holds: it covers no new edit; a new plan of these files restores or adapts the code
a plan file still holds the conflict markers git leaves in a merge it could not finish, so it is read as no plan and no protected edit passes until the merge is resolved

a decision of this plan holds a conflict (two answers a merge kept, below), so the plan covers no edit: ask the person which holds; their answer clears it, and the plan covers its edits again with no new yes
the branch's READY plan is another session's work: this session began with a new task and made no record on that plan, so its edits are not that plan's
this command sets, exports or unsets a variable the host sets for this session (which session, project or host process a verb acts for), so it would act as another one: run it without that
the person kept, since their yes, a decision this READY plan was to replace, so that yes covers no edit: ask them; their yes again, in their words, covers the plan as it is now
the READY plan grew past the level the person's yes was given at, so it covers no edit until it holds that level's rows
the first write the gate allowed under the plan
the plan first became READY: its flow so far, as numbers
the plan was closed: its flow since READY, as numbers
the session was shown the branch's draft as the work in progress: what it lacks and the one call that shows it
the person set this plan aside: it is kept as history and covers nothing
the plan states that the task leaves no further fork, with its reason: it stands for the forks the level asks beyond the ones found
the gate's denial named the one plain question to ask the person
not a record this version knows
a text field holds what looks like a secret, and .decisionbook/ is committed: nothing of this call was written; say where the secret is kept (a variable's name, a vault path), never its value

a question of this plan is still unanswered, so its title may name a part that was left out and is not the commit's subject: run the close again with --subject "<what shipped, in one line>"; nothing was written

this branch holds a plan an earlier session left open, so no new plan is started beside it: go on with it (a READY one is frozen: build from it; a draft: the session start named its one call); is its work done, ask the person whether to close it (atlasbound decisionbook close <id>), never close it to get past this; where the person's new decision replaces or keeps one of that plan's, send this new with that decision naming it ("supersedes" or "keeps":["<its id>/<key>"]): it opens beside it; other work is planned beside it: send this new again with the files it plans, and ask the person nothing about that plan
setting a plan aside is the person's: "said" quotes their own words that set it aside, from a message they typed in this session; if they have not said so, ask them
"no further fork" says why in a sentence: what you looked for and why the task leaves the person no choice there; a choice it does leave is a question instead
a no-fork item speaks of a file the plan plans ("file": a planned path, its plans link before it): what you read in that file and why nothing in it is open
the plan wrote a question to the person: a behaviour the task and the code leave open

a question that asks leave to edit a file the plan already names is no fork: the person's yes to the plan covers its files; ask only what the task leaves open, or state that no further fork is left (an item of kind no-fork, with why)
this record type is written by its own verb only
not a node: write type:value (plan, decision, file, test, issue, commit, handoff)
research comes before any question to a person: add a research record first

a person already decided this fork on these files, or the question names their decision: build on that decision; only the person changes it: a decision of theirs that names it in "supersedes", their own words in "said"
"supersedes" and "keeps" name a standing decision as <plan id>/<key>, this plan's own or another plan's (atlasbound decisionbook show decision:<key> prints it), and this is none
the question restates the task: ask what the plan cannot go on without, the fork the code cannot settle

this key already holds a person's decision here, or a conflict this answers: the answer places every line of it: name all of these in "supersedes", or the one line whose decision the person takes as it is in "keeps" (its value copied as this answer's) and every other in "supersedes", and send it again

this answer ends a conflict, and no replace question naming every line of it was on record before the person typed these words: record that question first, in a call of its own ({"t":"question", "supersedes": all of these}), ask them saying each line, who and their words, then record the answer they type after it to that question
a compared link is a plan's own person's answer to that plan's item, so a teammate's plan's item is cleared by them, in their clone: record nothing on it here, and tell the person it waits for them

a teammate wrote the line that stands for this key here, and only the one who wrote a line changes it in place. The person's decision goes in a plan of this machine's own (one `atlasbound decisionbook new` naming its files), under the same key, naming this one: "supersedes" where their words replace it, "keeps" where they keep it; both people's lines then stand in the records

the person decided this key in this plan, and only the person changes their decision: ask them; record their answer as theirs ("whose":"person", "said": their own words) naming it in "supersedes", or keep yours as a proposal ("proposed": true)
a decision that answers a question names its effect on the plan: effect ["file:<planned path>", "check:<id>" or "<item kind>:<item text>"]
research that settles a fork cites the file:line of this repository that settles it (source), and that line exists
a tool's answer (an MCP server, a web or documentation tool) is kept as a pointer to what it pointed at, never as research
the research rests on the AI's own reading: enough records cite a file read in the plan's sessions
fewer research records cite a file read in the plan's sessions than the level asks
a file of the repository read with the Read tool: a read receipt
a file of the repository a shell command named (cat, sed, grep, ...): a read receipt
a gap closed by evidence that cites a file:line of this repository (source) cites one that exists
a link says why it holds or where it comes from (why or source); a compared link says why: what the code holds, in short
a confirm is the person's yes to the plan: by names the person who said it, never the AI

a confirm is the person's yes, and no person's message came in this session after this plan was first written: send this call's other records again now without the confirm (their words stay on them), then show the person the plan and ask; their next message lets you record the yes (a new sends its plan without the confirm)
removing a link DecisionBook wrote (built-on, or the issue link) is the person's: by names the person who asked for it, never the AI
a plan of a version this one cannot read
say how success is seen (success) and what kind of work it is (kind)
research is your own reading: open the code yourself (Read, or cat, sed, grep on the file), then record what you found there with source <file>:<line>; a tool's answer is a pointer, never research
name the primary feature this changes (an item of kind feature)
plan the files or globs (plans links), each feature-scoped: two path segments before a wildcard
give at least one check a validation command
cover every check by a task (an item of kind task whose covers names it), and every task covers a check

a blocking question has no answer from a person yet: ask them its text in plain words, then record their decision answering it: "value" is what you understood they decided, "said" their own words, copied from their message; an assumption does not answer it

a person's standing decision of another plan holds on a file this plan edits, or stands beside its decision of the same key, or person decisions of one of its own keys stand beside each other, and this plan places it nowhere. Where this change does not touch what it decides, say why and ask nothing: {"t":"item","kind":"non-goal","text":"<why>","covers":["<ref>"]}. Only where the task goes against it, ask the person the replace question: a question with "supersedes":["<ref>"]; their answer names it in "supersedes" (it replaces it) or "keeps". What the person said of it (it stays, it changes) is never a non-goal: it is their decision naming it
a planned file in a danger zone has no decision whose files cover it
a planned new file goes where this repository does one thing two ways, and no person has decided the team's standard; asked once, a decision of its key in any plan closes it
name an actor or role (an item of kind actor)
add edge cases with their expected behaviour (items of kind edge)
record the cross-feature impact (an item of kind impact), and name every consumer item's text in an impact item's covers

a fork counts when research settles it citing file:line (settles), or a person's decision answers its question with an effect that lands in the plan. A question is only what the code cannot answer and a human must decide: a business or product rule, what a user, a customer or an operator will see, pay or lose, a trade-off of scope, cost or risk (decides, whyNotCode); read each file you will change for them, and never invent such a rule. An implementation choice is yours, never a question: state it as an assumption and show it with the plan. Never ask to reach the level's number: fewer forks than it hold once every question asked has their answer and each planned file has its own no-fork item saying what you read there and why nothing in it is a human's to decide: {"t":"item","kind":"no-fork","file":"<planned file>","text":"<what you read there; why it leaves the person no choice>"}; never leave to edit a planned file as a question
a bug needs repro evidence (an item of kind repro)
a user-interface change needs a precedent: how the repository already does it (an item of kind precedent)
critical work writes its risk (an item of kind risk)
critical work writes how to roll it back (an item of kind rollback)

the one rule of the yes: the person's typed answers to every blocking question are their yes, recorded by the product (record each as their decision). Their yes in words is asked only where that cannot be: the plan asks no blocking question, or one answer keeps a decision the plan was to replace; then show them the plan and ask, and record {"t":"confirm","by":"","said":"<their own words>"}
the level runs higher than proposed: code decides, going up is free
a waiver keeps the proposed level below a soft signal
not a small fix: it runs as normal work
no protected paths are configured in .decisionbook/config.json, so the DecisionBook gate checks nothing
not a write of a file in this repository, so the DecisionBook gate does not read it
a protected file, and no READY plan on this branch: plan it with one `atlasbound decisionbook new` (its fill-in: the plan pack, or atlasbound decisionbook plan <path>)

a danger path (a danger zone, a database schema or migration) outside the READY plan is the person's, once: they approve this write, or you add it to the plan ({"t":"link","rel":"plans","to":"file:<this path>","why":""} in an add) and ask them for their yes
a danger zone or schema file needs a READY plan of critical work: plan this path by name and run decisionbook ready again
this branch's plan is not READY yet, so it covers no edit
this change takes protection away from the protect policy, so the person says yes to it, every time
the protect policy in .decisionbook/config.json cannot be read, so every write asks the person until it is repaired
the protect policy holds a word the gate does not read; a misspelt protect would protect nothing, so the policy is not read
this changes a file only the person changes, so the person says yes to it, every time
this READY plan was not confirmed on this machine: the person says yes once to use it here

this session runs in a permission mode where the host lets an ask through with no one asked, so the gate cannot ask: tell the person what you want and why; they make the change themselves (atlasbound protect, in their own terminal, or an editor), or plan it again here with one `atlasbound decisionbook new`, or leave that mode and you try again
the person said yes to the gate's ask: this READY plan is used here from now on
no ask of the gate was waiting for this write
this shell command writes no file of this repository that the gate can name
the DecisionBook gate allows every file of this repository this shell command writes
a write this build cannot place; use Edit for it
the head this session began on and the protected files already changed then are kept on this machine, for its Stop
this session's start cannot be kept (no home or no session), so its Stop reads only what git's status names
every protected file this session changed is recorded by a READY or closed plan of this branch
protected files changed in this session and no READY or closed plan of this branch covers them: record this change in a plan (why, the decisions, the files) before you finish

this session's work under this READY plan is in the work tree and no close records it as it is now. Is the work finished? Run atlasbound decisionbook close with this plan's id (where less or other than its title shipped, add --subject "<what shipped, in one line>"), then give the person the one commit it prints, as printed. Is it not finished? Tell the person what is left. This is said once for the work tree as it is
the host already goes on because of a Stop block, so this Stop does not block again
taking protection away is the person's choice: they run it in their own terminal, where it asks them
the branch's READY plan was given to the session
only a draft plan is on this branch
nothing is protected here, so the DecisionBook gate checks nothing
the person said /resume-handoff: DecisionBook's shared part was added
no plan on this branch: the session was told so, with the plan pack of the prompt's area and the two calls that plan a code change first
the branch holds a draft plan: the session was told it is the work in progress, with its one next call, whatever the message's words
nothing to add to this prompt
the session was given the earlier plans of the prompt's area: the files it names, the branch changed or the session touched, their neighbours and concerns
the session was given the earlier plans of the area of a file it read or edited, the ones it had not been given yet
no earlier plan relates to this work
the session was given the promised surface of a file it read or edited: the import line a person or a plan promised, nothing else
a test file imports what no promise gives: the module bound whole under a promised name, or a file inside a promised folder; asked once a session and file, and a second write keeps it
what this session was given cannot be kept (no home or no session), so a file it touches gives nothing rather than the same cards again
what is protected and what could be
the person's answer is kept with its door and time
that answer cannot be kept here

words.packStated: A value the person's message sets, or says stays, is a decision at any level, unasked: {"t":"decision","key":"<area.topic>","value":"","why":"","whose":"<person | the teammate whose words the message gives>","said":"<the words, copied>"} in the new, by the rule of whose words a decision holds; of the same thing as a decision above: its key, naming it in "supersedes" (changed) or "keeps" (it stays; in that decision's own plan under a key of its own).
words.packCalls: If this request changes code: research first, no question yet ({first}the issue thread whole; past plans: this pack; a sideways search: git log of the files, the issues; then the code), fill every "" of this `new` (plan EVERY file you will change, tests included; add a record of a row you need more of; a question is only what the code cannot answer and a human must decide (a business or product rule; what a user or an operator sees, pays or loses; a trade-off), one each, never invented and never asked to reach a number: {"t":"question","q":"Q1","text":"","decides":"<area.topic>","whyNotCode":"","proposal":"<the answer you propose>","blocking":true}; an implementation choice is yours, stated, never asked: {"t":"assumption","text":"<what you will do>","why":""}; before the first question what the research answered, else it is refused: {"t":"research","tool":"read","asked":"","answer":"","source":"<file you read>"}) and send it once, before you ask the person anything and before your first edit; then show the person the plan, EVERY question in one message, each with your proposal, never the proposals as a whole, then your assumptions, and stop. Then record their answers in one add, a decision per question answered: "answers" its q, "value" what you understood they decided, whose words it holds and the words, by the rule of whose words a decision holds. A rule the issue, the repository or the person gives to someone else to decide (an owners table, "Emma will confirm", "that is Emma's call") is their question, never the person's: it carries "to":"<who>" and "source":"<where they are named>", waits for them without blocking, and the person may relay their answer. If it only asks or reads, go on.

unproven.no-source: these words are not in a message the person typed in this session, and the record gives no "source" to read them at: where the person told you them, copy the whole sentence from their message; where {who} wrote them (an issue, a comment), add "source": that address, and copy the words from there

words.whoseGuide:
Whose words a decision holds: one rule, for every decision you record from what the person writes: in the task message, in a later message, in an answer to a question. Credit a teammate only for words that are theirs; everything else is the person's own, or your assumption. The product takes words as a teammate's only where the message's format names the speaker (a chat line "Emma: …", a chat header, the > lines under "Emma wrote:"); for any other relay the host asks the person to Allow the list when you record it. One decision per thing decided: {"t":"decision","key":"<area.topic>","value":"<what was decided>","why":"","whose":"<person | a teammate's name | assumed>","said":"<the exact words>"}. An answer to a question carries "answers":"Q1" in place of "key" and "why", an "effect":["file:<a planned path>"], and no "value" where they took your proposal as it is. The product fills in who recorded it and where it was said; never add "by" or "saidBy". "said" is copied, never reworded: the words that decide; the product keeps the whole sentence they stand in.
1. "Emma says 7 days.", "BA confirmed: 7 days." or "I asked Emma and she told me: '7 days'" -> whose: Emma (or BA: the name or role as the person wrote it), said: "7 days". The same where no question was asked, as in a task message: "Build the export. Emma wants it capped at 500 rows." -> a decision in the new, whose: Emma, said: "Emma wants it capped at 500 rows".
2. A pasted chat, "Emma (BA) 11:42" then her lines -> whose: Emma, said: her line, copied. Her words end at the blank line after them: what the person writes below the paste is the person's own, or whose that sentence itself names.
3. "See Olivia's comment on the issue." -> read the comment; whose: Olivia, said: her words copied from it, plus "source": the comment's address (only an address is a source; a call or a chat is not).
4. "The rest as you proposed." -> whose: person, said: that sentence. It is the person's decision, never Emma's, though Emma answered other questions. It covers the open questions only: it never replaces ("supersedes") a decision someone else made.
5. "The PM changed the limit to 14." or "Olivia told me the minimum is dropped." -> whose: the PM, or Olivia (the one that sentence names, never the one a paste above it names), said: that sentence, "supersedes": the old decision, which stays on record. Someone else's decision is replaced only by a sentence that names what changes, as these do, or by the person's answer to a question that asked them about that decision by name.
6. "Yes, as a todo.", "Not sure yet." or "Ask me later." -> no decision: the person put the question off. Record that as what it is, {"t":"later","answers":"Q1","said":"<their words>"}: the question stays open, your proposal is not their decision, and nothing is built that waits on it. Tell the person it stays open. Where they did decide ("add a TODO comment in the code", "7 days, we revisit it later") it is a decision as any other; where you cannot tell which, ask them.
7. "Those are Emma's call, leave them parked for her." or "That one is Olivia's to answer." -> no decision: the question is theirs. Send each such question (again under its "q" where the plan holds it) with "to":"<the one the person named>" and "source":"<the person's sentence>": whom the person names outranks whom the issue names. With no plan on the branch yet, open one now with those questions (the new), also where nothing is built today: only a plan in the repository reaches a teammate's inbox and session start. A handoff note stays in the person's own home and hands nothing to a teammate.
A choice no one stated is "whose": "assumed", with no "said". A refusal says which words were not found where: copy them again from that place.
words.blanket: {lines}: the quoted words do not name this decision. Someone else's standing decision is replaced only on the person's words that name it (what it is about, its value, or the new value in full), or on their answer to a question that showed it to them (a question whose "supersedes" names it), typed after it was asked,: an answer to the open questions ("the rest as you proposed") replaces no decision someone else made. Take it out of "supersedes" and leave that decision as it stands; where the person does want it changed, ask them about it by name and record the words they answer with
